proof_summary: For the exceptional exponents, writing a number and its reversal modulo 27 or 81 via \(10^i\equiv1+9i\) gives \(S(9m-7)\equiv0\), forcing the digit sum \(S\) to be divisible by the modulus; the bounds \(m\le3\) and \(m\le9\) then force the only positive extremal candidates to be \(999\) and \(999999999\), while the case modulo 9 is immediate. For every larger exponent, the palindromic multiple \(29799999792\) of \(3^5\) is repeatedly concatenated threefold, gaining a factor of 3 each time and producing a palindromic multiple of \(3^{5+p}\) with only \(11\cdot3^p<27\cdot3^p\) digits, hence strictly smaller than the corresponding all-nines number.
